title: Two unread cipher lines on the title page of ad-Dani's at-Taisir (Berlin, Ms. or. oct. 3629)

documents.shelfmark: Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin, Orientabteilung, Ms. or. oct. 3629, f. 1a
documents.date: 21 Rabi' II 615 AH (July 1218), date of copying. The cipher lines are undated.
documents.route: unknown (written on the title page of a manuscript; no addressee)

plaintext.source: No reading exists; Sellheim 1976 reproduces the lines without one.

transcription.source: Sellheim, VOHD XVII A 1 (1976), Tafel 55 Abb. 69, SBB digital page image PPN1879946874-00000461
transcription.notes: Printed halftone, signs 25 to 40 px high. 40 signs seen against Sellheim's 43(?); six present but not classed; the 18 classes are shape groups and several are unsafe. The distinct count includes the unclassed mark.

system.summary: Two lines of separate signs, many with dots or loops beneath, on an Arabic title page; system not identified.
system.notes: Signs fit in part three families: Arabic digits with zero marks (the abjad numeral cipher of Sellheim Abb. 92), Coptic cursive numerals, Coptic letters. None gives a reading on the plate.

prior_solution.where: Sellheim 1976 gives no reading; none found in DECODE, Tomokiyo, Lasry's key list or by web search (15 and 16 Nov 2026).

conditions.human_role: Set the goal "solve this cipher" with the catalogue page of no. 2886; no target-specific intervention.

solution.what: Downloaded Sellheim's Tafel 55 (Abb. 69), Tafel 59 (Abb. 92) and pp. 23, 176-177 from SBB digital. The manuscript leaf was not reached: qalamos.net and orient-digital reset the connection, the Leipzig mirrors did not connect, the Wayback Machine has no copy.
Read the cipher of Abb. 92 (Ms. or. oct. 3938, about 1800) against the clear note above it: abjad values written as Arabic digits with one loop beneath per zero, right to left.
Cropped, enlarged and descreened the two lines; classed 40 signs into 18 shape classes with six left unclassed (signs.txt).
Counts: the 9-shaped sign and the loop-with-stroke sign four times each; one adjacent doubled sign at the start of line 2; a bigram recurring eight signs apart in line 1.

Arabic digits with zero marks and abjad values, as in Abb. 92: several digit shapes match and line 1 could open m-l-k, but the continuation and the opening of line 2 give no words, and the bare 9 would be ta' four times.

Coptic cursive numerals with abjad values, compared with the Pihan, Mallon and Megally tables (WG2 N3843) and a Noto Sans Coptic chart: partial shape matches, a possible "'Abd al-Latif" across the line break that needs three signs read against their shape.

Coptic letters, read left to right (Coptic, or Arabic in Coptic letters) and right to left with Greek-order numeral values; also mirrored and inverted views for disguised Arabic letters. Nothing reads.

Pattern cribs: the scribe's name, ibn ... ibn, bi-llah, wa-llah, 'Abd Allah, 'afa llahu 'anhu, ya kabikaj, wa-ma tawfiqi illa bi-llah, milk al-faqir. bi-llah and wa-llah fit the first five signs of line 2 but cannot be carried through.

Scribe's name on the Abb. 92 system: line 1 laid out as milk Abu Sa'id [ibn] Humaid. Five sign values fit their shapes, about as many are forced (the 9-shape as ya', R as 'ayn), the spacing of the two ya'-dal pairs is two signs too long, and the continuation does not align with ash-Shafi'i al-Muqri'.
Tested positional Arabic letter forms in 423,869 windows from the Quran and al-Taysir under four reading arrangements. No window matched all repeated signs in the provisional 21+22 transcription.

outcome.method_basis: No reading and no key: the system is not identified, and the sign classes cannot be made safe on the printed halftone.

gaps.item: The whole text, 40 to 43 signs on f. 1a
gaps.detail: Only a printed halftone was available; zero dots, loops and sign boundaries cannot be told apart on it. Needs a scan of the leaf.

gaps.item: Seven signs repeated in the margin of f. 72b
gaps.detail: Not reproduced by Sellheim; Qalamos not reachable from this network.

outcome.notes: Two lines remain unread. Comparisons with historical alphabets and searches of Arabic texts yielded no verified reading. Sellheim reports seven signs on folio 72b that could test a proposed key. See research-2026-11.md for evidence and limitations.
